name: Games, Auctions and Poker
description: Find equilibria, bid in auctions and size poker bets the way trading interviews ask.

requires.why: Uses expected value of a bet to compute payoffs and mixed-strategy mean outcomes.
Solves two simultaneous equations to find a 2 by 2 mixed equilibrium.
Reuses the V equals max(stop, go on) recursion to solve sequential games by backward induction.
Explains adverse selection to motivate the winner's curse in common-value auctions.
Bid shading maximises expected profit by setting a derivative to zero.
Uses backward induction and Kelly sizing from the puzzles games and betting lessons.
Counts poker hands and uses the probability rules from the poker-hands lesson.

lessonNames.l7-guess-two-thirds: Guess two thirds of the average

lessonObjectives.l1-payoff-tables: Write a two-player game as a payoff table and read each player's best reply.
lessonObjectives.l2-dominated-moves: Remove dominated strategies until the game is small.
lessonObjectives.l3-nash-equilibrium: Find the pure equilibria and say why neither player wants to move.
lessonObjectives.l4-mixing: Find a mixed equilibrium by making the opponent indifferent.
lessonObjectives.l5-zero-sum: Value a zero-sum game by its minimax mixed strategy.
lessonObjectives.l6-game-trees: Solve a sequential game by backward induction and spot threats nobody would carry out.
lessonObjectives.l7-guess-two-thirds: Iterate best replies and see why real players stop early.
lessonObjectives.l8-sealed-bids: Compare first-price and second-price auctions and bid well in each.
lessonObjectives.l9-winners-curse: Shade a bid for a common-value prize, because winning is bad news.
lessonObjectives.l10-splitting-a-pie: Solve ultimatum and alternating-offer bargaining games.
lessonObjectives.l11-pot-odds: Call or fold by comparing your chance of winning with the price of the call.
lessonObjectives.l12-ranges: Estimate your chance of winning against a range of hands.
lessonObjectives.l13-toy-poker: Find the best bluffing and calling frequencies in a three-card poker game.
lessonObjectives.l14-value-of-information: Price information as the expected gain from deciding after seeing it.
lessonObjectives.l15-sizing-and-risk: Compare expected value, expected log wealth and risk of ruin when sizing a bet.
